public_rationale: Two parts hold. AI startups were raising money in rounds of several hundred million dollars: Replit raised $250M and Cognition over $400M in September 2025. In August 2025, TechCrunch reported 'very negative' gross margins at AI coding startups such as Windsurf, which sold itself rather than stay independent. The claim that the group was 'floundering, struggling to stay alive' does not hold up as a general description. Replit's valuation nearly tripled as its annualised revenue rose from $2.8M to $150M in under a year. Gamma, an AI-native startup, said it had been profitable for over two years. Replit's own CEO said it was gross-margin positive.
limitations: 'AI startups' has no defined population, so a broad statement can fit some firms and not others.
Margin data for private firms are leaked or self-reported.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI startups other than OpenAI and Anthropic are floundering with negative gross margins.

statement.excerpt: Outside of these two, AI startups are floundering, struggling to stay alive and raising money in several-hundred million dollar bursts as their negative-gross-margin businesses flounder.

from_speaker: Outside of these two [OpenAI and Anthropic]
AI startups are floundering, struggling to stay alive
raising money in several-hundred million dollar bursts
our_interpretation: This is a generalisation about AI startups as a group, other than OpenAI and Anthropic. It is not a claim that every startup has negative margins.

The claim has three parts: (a) the startups raise money in rounds of several hundred million dollars; (b) their businesses have negative gross margins; (c) they are floundering and struggling to stay alive.
Target period: July 1 to September 29, 2025. His examples in the surrounding text refer to July and September 2025.
Margins that include the cost of free users fit his framing.
criteria.support_condition: Reports from the period show typical AI startups raising rounds of several hundred million dollars, with negative gross margins and signs of distress such as forced sales, shutdowns or emergency raises.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reports from the period show leading AI startups with positive margins or profits, rising valuations and fast revenue growth rather than struggles to survive.

evidence.excerpt: Vibe coders generally, and Windsurf in particular, can have such expensive structures that their gross margins are “very negative,” one person close to Windsurf told TechCrunch.
evidence.explanation: Supports the negative-gross-margin part, at least for AI coding startups, a large group of AI apps. The same article reports that Windsurf sold itself rather than stay independent.

evidence.excerpt: Replit said on Wednesday it has raised $250 million in a funding round that values the San Francisco-based company at $3 billion
evidence.explanation: Supports the 'raising money in several-hundred million dollar bursts' part. The same report notes Cognition raised over $400 million that week.

evidence.excerpt: Replit was valued at just over $1 billion in 2023 after it raised $97.4 million. The company said its annualized revenue rose to $150 million from $2.8 million in less than a year.
evidence.explanation: A nearly tripled valuation and revenue growth from $2.8M to $150M annualised in under a year do not fit 'floundering, struggling to stay alive' for one of the leading AI startups.

evidence.excerpt: Gamma has been profitable for over two years and has achieved its revenue milestone, having initially raised only $23 million.
evidence.explanation: A profitable AI-native startup that did not depend on large funding rounds during the period. It cuts against the claim that AI startups as a group were struggling to survive on negative margins.

evidence.excerpt: He also said that unlike many AI-powered coding companies, Replit is gross margin positive.
evidence.explanation: Replit's CEO says the company is gross-margin positive, while saying 'many' rivals are not. Dated just after the period and self-reported, so context only.
